items.snippet: SpaceX未来数月将推进IPO计划，正式开启上市进程。
items.raw_snippet: In the coming months, space and technology company [SpaceX has an opportunity to dethrone Saudi Aramco](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/01/01/10-stock-market-predictions-for-2026/?utm_source=globeandmail&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=article&referring_guid=06f0e74d-0d8f-4d07-a864-8eb629085238). According to reports from Bloomberg News and Reuters on April 1, billionaire Elon Musk's SpaceX has confidentially filed for a [U.S. IPO](https://www.fool.com/investing/stock-market/types-of-stocks/ipo-stocks/?utm_source=globeandmail&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=article&referring_guid=06f0e74d-0d8f-4d07-a864-8eb629085238). It would give them access to the [lucrative space industry](https://www.fool.com/investing/stock-market/market-sectors/industrials/space-stocks/?utm_source=globeandmail&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=article&referring_guid=06f0e74d-0d8f-4d07-a864-8eb629085238) (including Starlink), along with xAI, the artificial intelligence (AI) company behind large language model Grok, which merged with SpaceX in February of this year. Whereas automakers typically trade at high single-digit or low double-digit P/E ratios, [Tesla has consistently been valued at a triple-digit P/E ratio](https://www.fool.com/investing/2025/12/25/5-beloved-stocks-on-wall-street-id-sell-right-now/?utm_source=globeandmail&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=article&referring_guid=06f0e74d-0d8f-4d07-a864-8eb629085238). As other Musk-owned businesses, such as SpaceX and xAI, have rapidly grown, [Tesla's sales growth has ground to a halt](https://www.fool.com/investing/2024/02/26/opinion-the-tesla-growth-story-is-officially-dead/?utm_source=globeandmail&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=article&referring_guid=06f0e74d-0d8f-4d07-a864-8eb629085238). With the understanding that we don't yet have a prospectus to mull over, [it takes a lot of capital](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/03/31/individual-investors-rare-buy-spacex-ipo/?utm_source=globeandmail&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=article&referring_guid=06f0e74d-0d8f-4d07-a864-8eb629085238)*and* time to build reusable rockets and Starship vehicles, satellites for Starlink's network, and data centers for xAI. The [stock market entered 2026 at its second-priciest valuation in history](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/01/10/stock-market-3-times-155-years-history-what-next/?utm_source=globeandmail&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=article&referring_guid=06f0e74d-0d8f-4d07-a864-8eb629085238), according to the Shiller P/E Ratio.

items.raw_snippet: That was the organizing message from IPWatchdog LIVE 2026’s session: *The Business Impact of AI in Practice: Calculating ROI in the AI Era.* The panel featured Stephanie Curcio (NLPatent), Bernard Tomsa (Brooks Kushman), Bruce Berman (The Center for Intellectual Property Understanding), and Francesca Cruz (Juristat). Curcio introduced the session’s most durable contribution: a three-part framework for evaluating AI ROI in professional IP practice quantity, quality, and quanta. The practices that will define the next decade are those that measure what their tools actually deliver, restructure their value proposition around quanta rather than speed, and recognize that the most powerful thing AI does for an IP professional is not making existing work faster, but rather making previously impossible work achievable. ##### AI, Budget Cuts, and the Future of In-House Patent Teams | *IPWatchdog Unleashed*. ##### Webinar: From Patent Tools to AI Agents – The Next Evolution of Patent Practice. ##### Webinar: Beyond Patent Data – Unifying IP and R&D with AI-Driven Intelligence.

items.snippet: **Part 1: What I Learned the Hard Way in My First Board Meeting as a Technology ...
items.raw_snippet: **Part 1: What I Learned the Hard Way in My First Board Meeting as a Technology Leader**. I use a simple framework I call E³: *Explore, Experiment, Execute.*. If your board can walk out remembering three words, they can ask better questions and hold the right people accountable. A framework like the Macro Process Wheel gives leadership a common language for identifying which processes AI will touch, how the work inside them will change, and what dependencies that creates. The organizations that skip Explore and Experiment and rush straight to Execute often build the wrong things at scale. The best technology leaders I know treat Explore like a learning cost, experiment like a bounded bet, and Execute like a capital commitment that requires the same rigor as any other major investment. ☀️ Subscribe to the **Early Morning Byte!** Begin your day informed, engaged, and ready to lead with the latest in technology news and thought leadership.

items.title: The new investing edge might be hiding in firms' own data
items.snippet: # The new investing edge might be hiding in firms' own data. With top funds hoov...
items.raw_snippet: # The new investing edge might be hiding in firms' own data. With top funds hoovering up as much publicly available data as possible with AI, investors say the next market-beating edge will come from searching their own research, communications, and historical decisions for signals competitors can't access. AI is "great at structuring unstructured data," said Jacob Bowers, a vice president of quantitative research at BlackRock, on a panel at the Future Alpha conference in New York on Tuesday, and "some of the best unstructured data you have is internal.". The publicly accessible data that was once cutting-edge is now "commoditized" by AI, he said. Andrew Gelfand, a quant at Balyasny focused on alpha capture, said at the Future Alpha conference that the firm had previously tried to monetize unstructured data within the firm's systems, but recent AI advances have made the task much more fruitful.

items.raw_snippet: As firms adopt these technologies to increase efficiency, enhance insights, and accelerate deal execution, a critical question arises: **Is AI replacing human investment bankers, or is it transforming their roles entirely?**. Despite the undeniable power of AI to transform workflows, there are several aspects of investment banking where human skills remain essential. As AI automates many traditional analyst tasks, the role of investment banking professionals, especially early‑career analysts, is shifting toward higher‑value responsibilities. An investment banking course that incorporates modern tools and teaches students to work with AI accelerates this transition and prepares learners for future‑ready roles. As investment banking evolves, the narrative that AI will fully replace human bankers is oversimplified. By pursuing structured learning, such as an investment banking course that combines finance fundamentals with exposure to modern tools, aspiring professionals can position themselves for success in a landscape where human intelligence and artificial intelligence work together synergistically. Salesforce plans to hire 2,000 new salespeople to focus on selling artificial intelligence (AI) products as the company planning to expand its AI offerings. ### Salesforce to Hire 2,000 Salespeople for AI Expansion. A month ago, Benioff mentioned that Salesforce would hire 1,000 new salespeople for AI roles. Salesforce aims to make AI a key part of its product lineup, with AI tools to help sales teams, marketers, and customer service agents do their jobs more efficiently. The new salespeople will help introduce and sell Salesforce’s latest AI technology, including the upcoming second version of its Agentforce platform. This software is designed to create AI-powered agents to handle complex tasks, like answering questions in Salesforce’s Slack app using all available data. Benioff is very excited about Salesforce’s potential for AI. In a recent interview, he shared, *“I’ve never been more excited about anything at Salesforce, maybe in my career.”* He added that he expects the company to have over a billion AI agents within the next year. ### Salesforce’s AI Push Following 2022 Layoffs. Salesforce’s move into AI comes after the company laid off over 7,000 employees in 2022. After studying computer science at the **University of Cambridge**, where he was also a **member of the Young Entrepreneurs Society**, William went on to conduct research into automatic speech recognition at the GEC Hirst Research Centre. At Amazon, William became **Principal Product Manager for Alexa and the Echo**, playing a central role in advancing voice-activated technology. His standing in the field was recognised in 2019 when he was elected a **Fellow of the Royal Academy of Engineering**, alongside his fellowship with the Creative Destruction Lab in both Canada and the UK. ### Publications and Impact. items.raw_snippet: * English Content Revolut founder set to launch venture capital fund powered by artificial intelligence. # Revolut founder set to launch venture capital fund powered by artificial intelligence. Revolut founder Nik Storonsky is set to launch his own venture capital fund, powered by artificial intelligence. The new venture — dubbed QuantumLight Capital — will be worth around $200 million, with funds supplied by Storonsky and other investors, Forbes reported on Tuesday. “We are built as a technology company by a team of tech unicorn founders, quant traders, AI scientists and engineers,” the QuantumLight website states. The fund will identify investment opportunities using a machine called Aleph as its “proprietary quantitative decision engine.”. According to Forbes, QuantumLight will be focused mainly on Series B and Series C rounds, based on software which eliminates “human judgement.” Storonsky argues that the model is designed to eliminate the clubby world of venture capital, where decisions are made through a crowd mentality. The neobank founder has spent the last year building a team of data scientists and engineers to browse LinkedIn, corporate filings and other public databases in order to identify fast-growing startups. He will also hire in a CEO to head up the fund, according to the Forbes report. The move comes at a time of global expansion for Revolut. In recent months it has acquired banking licenses in at least 10 European countries as it has touted adding new products to it roster, such as home loans and buy-now-pay-later. It has also tussled with UK regulators over anti-money laundering requirements for its crypto products. It is still on the Financial Conduct Authority’s so-called temporary register, alongside crypto custodian Copper and three other firms. The register is a stopgap measure the FCA created after missing an earlier deadline to green-light companies’ operations. Their fate remains uncertain, but without full registration they could in theory be forced to stop crypto-related activities in the UK. ##### Relative altcoin weakness masks early internal rotation. ##### Block Scholes crypto options data comes to Bloomberg terminal to ‘Build Bridge’ for financial institutions. ##### China’s solar energy set to overtake coal, but new coal rush threatens ‘historic’ shift.

Illia Polosukhin, Co-Founder, NEAR Protocol (Stephen Lovekin/Shutterstock/CoinDesk). According to a deck reviewed by CoinDesk, the company is planning to hire AI engineers “soon,” and its product team is working to plan AI workstreams over a 3-6 month transition phase. This comes as the intersection between AI and blockchain continues to be a hot topic, with NEAR attempting to position itself at the forefront. Polosukhin was on a panel at Nivida’s conference titled "Transforming AI" last month, and saw its token NEAR double in price in anticipation of the event. The company is well seasoned in terms of AI expertise, Polosukhin is an artificial intelligence researcher and software engineer that co-built the ‘Transformer’ architecture.
